artifact_review: The Router identified two minor artifacts: slight edge softness on wings (severity 1.2) and melted flower petals under the butterfly (severity 1.5). I agree with these assessments. The 'melted' flower structure is a common generative weakness in complex, repetitive organic textures when occluded. The edge softness is borderline between AI artifact and realistic depth-of-field blur, but given the sharpness of the rest of the image, it leans slightly toward artifact. The experts did not find additional structural defects; the high mask confidence (0.95) confirms good boundary integrity despite the slight softness noted by the Router.
alignment_reasoning: The image demonstrates excellent class conformance. The fine_grained_classifier confirmed 'ringlet' with high confidence (logit 7.71 vs 3.43 for next best). All testable checkpoints (antennae, wing pattern, body shape, coloration) are present and correct. The only missing checkpoint (forelegs) is legitimately untestable. The alignment is near-perfect for a generated image of this complexity.
artifact_reasoning: The image is structurally sound with no catastrophic failures. However, minor generative artifacts are present. The flower head beneath the butterfly shows signs of 'melting' or structural collapse in the florets (severity ~1.5), lacking the crisp individual tube structures of a real composite flower. There is also very slight edge bleeding/softness on the wing margins (severity ~1.2). These issues prevent a perfect artifact score but do not significantly detract from the overall realism. The scores are calibrated against Reference 3 (Brambling, artifact 4.0), noting that the flower artifact here is slightly more noticeable than typical noise, hence the lower score.
